e112f5f5e794f1f39fcc.en: Newtalk News French high school students protested against the lack of educational resources, and the third wave of national demonstrations will be launched on the 6th. The movement initially sought to improve learning conditions such as school buildings and teacher manpower, but the actions were accompanied by destruction and violence, which have caused huge losses and personal injuries. Following the two waves of mass mobilization on September 29 and October 1, high school students and college students organized a call for the launch of "Act 3" on the 6th. Approximately 30 cities across the country participated, with varying times of action. In Paris, demonstrations will take place at Place de la République at 2 p.m. Students protested against dilapidated school buildings, overcrowded classrooms, teacher absences and lack of substitutes, overcrowded schedules, and the lack of transparency in Parcoursup, the university application system, and demanded that the state invest more human and financial resources in education to achieve more equitable education.
